title: 第九章 暗涌
content_zh:
那一夜寒风中的突破，并未给陈默的生活带来立竿见影的改变。胸口那堵“墙”依然厚重，暖流每日冲击，那夜挤出的缝隙依旧细微难辨，但陈默能感觉到，运行周天时，暖流在胸口盘桓的滞涩感，似乎真的减轻了那么一丝。很微弱，就像冬日冻土表面一道几乎看不见的裂痕，但底下，或许已有生机在缓慢萌动。

    他将这感受仔细记录在日课纸背面：“四月十七，酷寒。吐纳，气冲膻中，似有隙，行寸许，力竭退。瓶颈微有松动，然不彰。”

    字迹依旧工整，力透纸背，但“似有隙”三个字，笔锋隐约多了一丝不易察觉的锐利。

    倒春寒持续了三四日，才渐渐回暖。山道上的冰凌化了，屋檐滴滴答答落着水。杂役们冻裂的手脚开始发痒，通铺里的霉味混着劣质冻疮药膏的气味，更加难闻。但好歹，日子似乎又回到了往日那种沉重却稳定的轨道。

    陈默的柴刀更加锋利，黑铁磨石在他夜复一夜的打磨下，边缘光滑趁手，中间也磨出了便于握持的凹槽。那块大铁砧的平整面，则被他用收集来的、更细碎的金属块和砂石，混合着溪水，耐心打磨得几乎可以照出模糊的人影。虽然粗糙，但他试过，用柴刀在上面轻轻一蹭，刃口便能得到极好的修整。

    体术残篇的前两式，他坚持的时间越来越长。第一式已能稳住近三十息，第二式也突破了十息。每次练习，筋骨的酸痛依旧剧烈，但酸痛过后，那种仿佛淤塞被冲开、力量沉淀下来的感觉，也日益清晰。他依旧每隔几日，服用极微量的铁骨草汁液，胃部的不适感已大大减轻，或许是他的身体在适应，也或许是他处理得比最初更仔细些。

    他开始尝试第三式。这是一个需要单足站立，另一腿向后高高踢起，同时上身竭力前俯，双臂如翼展开的古怪姿势，对平衡、柔韧和核心力量的要求达到了新的高度。第一次尝试，他只摆出一半架势，就失去平衡摔倒在地，脚踝传来一阵刺痛。

    他没有冒进，只是更加耐心地从基础站姿和简单的拉伸开始，一点点增加难度。他知道，急不来。

    这日清晨，陈默砍完柴下山，在山道拐角处，又遇到了那个女孩。

    她依旧挎着那个破旧的竹篮，篮子里装着小半篮沾着露水的野菜和几株不起眼的草药。看见陈默，她愣了一下，随即低下头，加快脚步，似乎想从他身边匆匆走过。

    陈默脚步未停，目光在她篮子里扫了一眼。野菜很新鲜，但那几株草药，依旧是年份很浅的清心草和宁神花幼苗，在晨光下显得蔫蔫的。

    就在两人即将擦肩而过时，女孩忽然停下，转过身，从篮子里抓起两把最水灵的野菜，飞快地塞到陈默背着的柴捆上，然后不等陈默反应，扭头就跑，瘦小的身影很快消失在下方山道的树丛后。

    陈默停下脚步，看了看柴捆上那两把还带着湿泥和露珠的野菜。翠绿，鲜嫩，是山蕨菜最嫩的尖芽。他没说什么，只是将野菜拿起，小心地放在自己怀里，然后继续下山。

    午间，他将这两把野菜在溪水里洗净，就着凉水，慢慢吃了。很嫩，微微的涩味后是野菜特有的清甜。他吃得很干净，连根茎上细小的须都没放过。

    他想起那女孩逃跑时微微泛红的耳根，和篮子里那几株蔫头耷脑的药草。青云山脉外围，低阶灵草本就难寻，何况她一个没有修为的凡人女孩。能采到这些，不知要在山林里钻多久，冒多少风险。

    那八枚铜板，或许能让她和她的家人，多吃几顿饱饭。但之后呢？

    陈默吃完最后一口野菜，用袖子擦了擦嘴。目光投向远方雾气缭绕的群山。那里是宗门划定的、相对安全的区域之外，更深、更危险的山林。据说，更好的药材，更罕见的灵物，甚至是一些低阶妖兽，都在那些地方。但也意味着更多的危险，不仅是来自野兽和险峻地形，更可能来自其他同样在边缘挣扎的采药人、散修，甚至是……心怀叵测的同门。

    他收回目光，将脑海里那些模糊的念头压下。那些，离现在的他还太远。

    午后，陈默被派去清理练功坪边缘的杂草。练功坪是外门弟子日常修炼、较技的场所，以青石铺就，颇为宽阔。此时坪上正有几十名青衣外门弟子，或独自打坐吐纳，或三两成群练习基础法术，呼喝声、法术爆裂的轻微噼啪声不绝于耳。

    陈默和其他几个杂役，在坪子最外围，埋头清理着石缝和边缘土地里顽强生长的野草。他们低眉顺眼，动作麻利，尽量不去打扰那些修炼中的弟子，也尽量不引起他们的注意。

    陈默挥动着小锄，将一丛丛狗尾草连根掘起。泥土的气息混合着青草汁液的味道，弥漫在空气中。他偶尔抬眼，瞥向坪中。
content_en:
The breakthrough in the cold wind that night did not bring immediate changes to Chen Mo's life.The "wall" on his chest was still thick, and the warm current hit him every day, and the gap squeezed out that night was still subtle and difficult to distinguish, but Chen Mo could feel that the stagnant feeling of warm current lingering in his chest when he was running around seemed to have really lightened up a little.It's very faint, like an almost invisible crack on the surface of frozen soil in winter, but underneath, life may be slowly sprouting.

He carefully recorded this feeling on the back of the daily lesson paper: "April 17, it is extremely cold. Breathing in and out, the breath rushes into the body, and there seems to be a gap. After walking for an inch, it retreats after exhaustion. The bottleneck is slightly loosened, but it is not noticeable."

The handwriting is still neat and neat, penetrating through the back of the paper, but the word "seems to have gaps" has a slightly subtle sharpness to it.

The late spring cold lasted for three or four days before gradually getting warmer.The ice on the mountain road has melted, and water is dripping from the eaves.The handymen's frozen hands and feet began to itch, and the musty smell in the shop was mixed with the smell of inferior frostbite ointment, making it even more unpleasant.But at least, life seems to have returned to the heavy but stable track of the past.

Chen Mo's hatchet was even sharper. After he polished it night after night, the black iron whetstone made the edge smooth and easy to hold, and a groove was also ground in the middle for easy holding.The flat surface of the large anvil was polished patiently with the finer metal blocks and sand he collected, mixed with stream water, until a blurry silhouette of a human figure could almost be seen.Although it was rough, he tried it and rubbed it lightly with a hatchet, and the edge could be perfectly trimmed.

He persisted in the first two moves of the Taishu Fragment for longer and longer.The first posture has been able to stabilize for nearly thirty breaths, and the second posture has also exceeded ten breaths.Every time I practice, the pain in my muscles and bones is still severe, but after the pain passes, the feeling as if the blockage has been washed away and the strength has settled becomes increasingly clear.He still takes a very small amount of Iron Bone Grass juice every few days, and the discomfort in his stomach has been greatly alleviated. Perhaps his body is adapting, or perhaps he is handling it more carefully than at first.

He started to try the third form.This is a weird posture that requires standing on one foot, kicking the other leg high back, and at the same time bending the upper body forward as hard as possible and spreading the arms like wings. The requirements for balance, flexibility and core strength have reached a new height.On the first try, he only got half of the stance before he lost his balance and fell to the ground, feeling a sharp pain in his ankle.

He did not rush forward, but started with more patience from basic stances and simple stretches, gradually increasing the difficulty.He knew there was no rush.

Early that morning, Chen Mo went down the mountain after chopping firewood. At the corner of the mountain road, he met the girl again.

She was still carrying the worn bamboo basket, which contained a small half basket of dew-stained wild vegetables and a few inconspicuous herbs.Seeing Chen Mo, she was stunned for a moment, then lowered her head and quickened her pace, as if she wanted to rush past him.

Chen Mo didn't stop and glanced at her basket.The wild vegetables were very fresh, but the few herbs were still very young young seedlings of Chrysanthemum sinensis and Ningshen flower, which looked wilted in the morning light.

Just when the two were about to pass each other, the girl suddenly stopped, turned around, grabbed two handfuls of the juiciest wild vegetables from the basket, and quickly stuffed them onto the bundle of firewood carried by Chen Mo. Then, without waiting for Chen Mo to react, she turned around and ran away, and her thin figure quickly disappeared behind the trees on the mountain road below.

Chen Mo stopped and looked at the two handfuls of wild vegetables still covered with wet mud and dew on the bundle of firewood.Emerald green and fresh, it is the tenderest tip bud of mountain bracken.He didn't say anything, just picked up the wild vegetables, carefully placed them in his arms, and then continued down the mountain.

At noon, he washed these two handfuls of wild vegetables in the stream, soaked them in cold water, and ate them slowly.Very tender, with a slight astringency followed by the unique sweetness of wild vegetables.He ate it very cleanly, even the tiny whiskers on the roots.

He thought of the girl's slightly red ears when she ran away, and the few withered herbs in the basket.On the outskirts of the Qingyun Mountains, low-level spiritual herbs are hard to find, let alone a mortal girl with no cultivation.To collect these, I don’t know how long I have to dig in the forest and how much risk I take.

Those eight copper coins might allow her and her family to eat a few more meals.But what happens after that?

Chen Mo finished the last bite of wild vegetables and wiped his mouth with his sleeve.Gaze towards the mist-shrouded mountains in the distance.There are deeper and more dangerous mountains and forests outside the relatively safe area designated by the sect.It is said that better medicinal materials, rarer spiritual objects, and even some low-level monsters are all in those places.But it also means more dangers, not only from wild beasts and dangerous terrain, but also from other herb collectors, casual cultivators, and even... fellow disciples with ulterior motives who are also struggling on the edge.

He looked away and suppressed the vague thoughts in his mind.Those are still too far away from who he is now.

In the afternoon, Chen Mo was sent to clean up the weeds on the edge of the training ground.The training ground is a place where outer sect disciples practice and compete on a daily basis. It is paved with bluestone and is quite spacious.At this time, there were dozens of Tsing Yi outer sect disciples on the ground, either meditating alone or practicing basic spells in groups of three or two. The sound of shouts and the slight crackle of spell bursts could be heard all the time.

Chen Mo and several other handymen were at the outermost edge of Pingzi, immersed in clearing away the weeds that grew stubbornly in the cracks between rocks and on the edge of the land.They lowered their eyebrows and moved quickly, trying not to disturb the disciples who were practicing and trying not to attract their attention.

Chen Mo wielded a small hoe and dug up clumps of foxtail grass by their roots.The smell of earth mixed with the smell of grass juice filled the air.He occasionally raised his eyes and glanced at Pingzhong.
